story.head: The Jets are rolling
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime in Dallas on Oct 22. The Stars (10-5-2) beat San Jose 4-3 on Saturday, and the Jets have won four straight. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Jets sixth (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth (tied for 13th).
This season, the Stars have outscored teams 48-39, but only 30-28 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 12-6, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Jets ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (3rd). They also create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd), and that sets up a fight with the Stars’ power play (1st), which could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (24th). The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st), play slow, tight games (lowest) and kill penalties well (1st). Dallas has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Stars wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones.

Kyle Connor (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, with eight goals in 13 games against Dallas since 2023-24. Mark Scheifele (4 G / 15 A / 19 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Winnipeg. Jason Robertson (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 17 GP) is next in line.

Stuart Skinner (6-4-3 / .883 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to start for Winnipeg, and Jake Oettinger (9-3-1 / .906 SV% in 13 GS) for Dallas. Skinner has a .850 save percentage in eight starts against the Stars, well under his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
